note_body: Clinical Case — Angiodysplasia (Heyde’s Syndrome) for 73-year-old male H.M. admitted 2025-11-19 after a mechanical fall. Reports 6-8 weeks of progressive fatigue, dyspnoea (NYHA II→III), lightheadedness, and pallor without overt GI bleeding. Family confirms pallor and breathlessness. Denies haematemesis, melena, PR bleeding, epistaxis, haematuria, easy bruising, abdominal pain, bowel changes, or constitutional symptoms. PMH: hypertension, type 2 diabetes (diet+metformin), CKD3a (eGFR ≈45). Meds: ramipril 5 mg OD, metformin 500 mg BD, atorvastatin 20 mg nocte, OTC multivitamin; no antiplatelets/anticoagulants. Past surgery: left inguinal hernia repair 30 years ago. Social: ex-smoker (20 pack-years, quit 10y), no alcohol, retired accountant living with wife. Exam: pale, HR 88, BP 130/78, systolic ejection murmur 3/6 at RUSB radiating to carotids, lungs clear, abdomen benign, no edema or bruising. Labs: Hb 102 g/L, microcytic indices (MCV 70 fL), platelets 328, WBC 10.5, ferritin 12 ng/mL, iron low/TIBC high, creatinine 1.2, LFTs normal, coagulation normal, FOBT positive. Imaging: ECG NSR, CXR clear. Upper endoscopy negative. Colonoscopy shows flat red lesions in caecum/ascending colon consistent with angiodysplasia. Capsule enteroscopy shows multiple proximal ileal angiodysplasias. Impression: chronic occult GI blood loss from angiodysplasia associated with aortic stenosis (Heyde’s syndrome).

sections.text: Cardio: exertional dyspnoea, no chest pain. GI: denies abdominal pain or visible bleeding; stool changes absent. GU: no hematuria. Neuro/MSK: fall without deficits.

sections.text: Pale but comfortable, vitals stable, 3/6 ejection systolic murmur radiating to carotids, lungs clear, abdomen benign, no edema or bruising, neuro intact.

sections.name: Diagnosis
sections.text: Chronic occult GI blood loss from colonic/small bowel angiodysplasia associated with aortic stenosis (Heyde’s syndrome).
